newsitem.title: CHINA: China prosecutors vow to nail police crimes.
newsitem.headline: China prosecutors vow to nail police crimes.

text.p: China's top prosecutors have vowed to crack down on crimes committed by police who abuse their power for personal gain, the China Youth Daily said on Thursday.

Procuratorial organs urgently needed to crack down on violations of the law by police, who sometimes accept bribes to turn a blind eye to crime, the newspaper quoted Deputy Procurator Liang Guoqing as saying at a conference in Beijing.
In the first 11 months of 1996, prosecutors filed 7,000 complaints against policemen for unlawful practices, the newspaper said without elaborating.
In the same period, prosecutors also protested against nearly 2,000 unjust court sentences, it said. It did not say how many of these sentences were overturned.

A Chinese court sentenced to death a senior police officer last September for embezzling 20.19 million yuan ($2.43 million) in what the state media said was China's biggest police corruption case since the 1949 communist takeover.

China's market-oriented economic reforms have created opportunities for officials to abuse their positions. President Jiang Zemin has repeatedly warned that corruption is the most serious threat to the power of the ruling Communist Party.
